key_insight: Analog hardware can support generative modeling if the model is redesigned around fixed physical dynamics, and the paper shows two mechanisms—time-varying parameters and hidden states—that reduce the expressivity gap.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical path to low-power on-device generation by matching model structure to hardware constraints, while quantifying the area, power, and precision tradeoffs needed for implementation.
method: Introduces Analog Interaction Systems (AIS), a unified framework for hardware-implementable dynamical systems.
Adds hardware-compatible flexibility via piecewise time-varying parameters and hidden physical states.
Trains with a Wasserstein GAN objective so models need not reproduce a specific trajectory during training.
evidence_signal: On MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, the oscillator-based AIS achieved FID scores of 27.6 and 80.8, and the authors estimate about 23 uJ per generated image with a 4-bit sparse architecture.
watch_item: The approach depends on sparse, low-bit quantized hardware and fixed analog dynamics, so performance may degrade as connectivity or precision constraints tighten in real devices.
paper_title: Generative Models on Analog Hardware with Dynamics
